chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) told me, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from al-Husayn ibn Sufyan al-Jariri, from Salam ibn Abi 'Umra al-Azdi, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbuz, from Abu al-Tufayl, that he heard the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, after me will be darkening, blind, doubt-causing tribulations in which none will remain except the sleeper. It was said: O Commander of the Believers, and what is the sleeper? He said: The one about whom people do not know what is in his self.

key_terms.مَا فِي نَفْسِهِ: what is in his self/inner state

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'sleeper' in the tribulations after Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In Maani al-Akhbar, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ali (AS) characterizing the post-caliphate era as an era of 'blind tribulations' where only the 'sleeper' (al-nawma) endures. This concept, central to Shia eschatology, denotes a state of *taqiyya* (strategic dissimulation) or inner ambiguity, where individuals conceal their true faith amidst widespread confusion and doubt. It highlights the survival strategy of the faithful who maintain inner conviction while outwardly appearing indistinguishable from the masses during times of political and religious turmoil.
